source.summary: GitHub Actions 'Embedder footprint' runs for PR #253 (branch fix/118-resource-drop at commit 7871f9bc17bb45e55ec2431a68730e9428d6b784, the merge of the PR head f64653a8f62a906a659ce938abb8c7835826b50a with main 501b27c95b5d1cab7264cbb519f791e661ce5abd; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45058016773 and 45058029076 against the branch and pull-request run 45057705991, which built the same merge tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #253 (#118, canon resource.drop for host-provided resources). The PR is confined to the component layer: telomere-component gains the linker destructor-registration API (ComponentLinker::register_import_resource_drop / register_import_resource_drop_async), the decoder keeps each imported instance declaration's TypeId so instantiation can build the ResourceId-to-destructor table (runtime/env.rs), and the runtime tracks host-issued own handles (runtime/canonical.rs, runtime/host.rs) so canon resource.drop resolves them and calls the registered destructor exactly once; telomere-component-wasi gains WasiState::drop_handle and registers destructors for its handle-issuing imports in the provider. The core telomere library is untouched, so the baseline, core, core-nosimd and core-jit configurations are byte-identical in both profiles (16 of 28 gated series unchanged). Growth is confined to the configurations that link the component runtime: in the release profile, stripped file +17,256 B (component), +25,144 B (wasi) and +25,176 B (wasi-threads), stripped .text +15,200 B, +21,712 B and +21,712 B; in the release-size profile, stripped file +9,936 B, +14,168 B and +14,184 B, stripped .text +8,320 B, +11,024 B and +11,024 B. wasi and wasi-threads grow more than component because they also link telomere-component-wasi (drop_handle plus the provider's destructor registrations); wasi-threads tracks wasi almost exactly (+32 B stripped file in release, +16 B in release-size) because the PR adds no threads-specific code. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, 'Size regression gate (#164)'.
